Pre-project governance and gated deliver.description_en:
As project leads, project managers must fully understand the work involved so that they can adapt and adjust accordingly. This online self-paced course explains common situational leadership models that can help optimize work processes and efforts, including models that focus on cross-cultural communication, motivation, and change within organizations. Participants will investigate complexity models that facilitate decision-making and development models that foster high-performing project teams.

 

Topics include:

- distinguishing between common situational leadership models
- identifying motivation and change models
- exploring project team development models

 

Notes:

This course is intended for all public servants, including those with or without project management experience. Materials are aligned with the PMBOK® Guide – Seventh Edition.

Completion of the 26 courses in the CAPM® course series can count towards the eligibility requirements for the Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM®) exam administered for a fee by the Project Management Institute (PMI).
 
The CAPM® exam is not administered by the Canada School of Public Service. Learners wishing to take the exam are responsible for validating their eligibility directly with PMI.
Pre-project governance and gated deliver.title_fr: CAPM® : Modèles courants de gestion de projets (TRN355)
Pre-project governance and gated deliver.description_fr:
En tant que responsables de projets, les gestionnaires de projet doivent comprendre pleinement les travaux en cause afin de pouvoir s'adapter et s'ajuster en conséquence. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre présente les modèles de leadership situationnel courants qui aident à optimiser les processus et les efforts liés au travail, y compris les modèles qui mettent l'accent sur la communication interculturelle, la motivation et le changement au sein des organisations. Les participantes et participants exploreront des modèles de complexité qui facilitent la prise de décisions et l'élaboration de modèles qui favorisent des équipes de projet à rendement élevé.

 

Sujets traités :

- faire la distinction entre les modèles de leadership situationnel courants;
- cerner les modèles de motivation et de changement;
- explorer les modèles de création d'équipes de projet.

 

Remarques :

Ce cours s'adresse à tous les fonctionnaires, qu'ils aient ou non de l'expérience en gestion de projet. Le matériel est conforme à la septième édition du Guide PMBOK®.

La réussite des 26 cours de série de cours CAPM® peut être prise en compte dans les conditions d’admissibilité à l’examen payant d’Associé certifié en gestion de projet (CAPM®) du Project Management Institute (PMI).
 
L’examen CAPM® n’est pas offert par l’École de la fonction publique du Canada. Les apprenants qui souhaitent le passer sont responsables de vérifier leur admissibilité directement auprès du PMI.

Digital product lifecycle and upstream d.description_en:
Making the switch to digital technologies requires taking a close look at core business processes, organizational governance and customer experiences. This online self-paced course assembles a playbook of best practices for digital transformation that focus on the customer, mobilize operational processes and sustain the employee experience during a period of change. · recognizing the operational elements of digital transformation

· supporting business model transformation

· identifying the four major components of implementing digital transformation

Enterprise digital architecture and inte.description_en:
As the world becomes increasingly digital, public service skill sets and service delivery must follow suit. This course provides a high-level overview of the Government of Canada Digital Standards, which constitute the cornerstone of the government's shift to digital and to becoming more agile, open and user-focused. Participants will consider the positive impacts of the government's digital standards on the everyday work of public servants and explore ways to adapt to new digital realities and mindsets.
 
Topics include:
 
·       understanding the current context and enablers of a digital government
·       defining the Government of Canada Digital Standards
·       recognizing digital behaviours in relation to the Digital Standards
·       applying the Digital Standards in the context of your work

· acknowledging the challenges of transforming to a DevOps culture

· reviewing examples of key strategies for DevOps success
